rounds.text: Arihant Capital Markets is currently demonstrating a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a 22% growth in trailing twelve-month sales [E17] and a robust 62% year-over-year increase in net profit [E66]. The company is fundamentally outperforming its sector peers, maintaining an ROA of 4.21% compared to the 1.94% benchmark [E8], and an ROCE of 12.03% against the sector’s 5.66% [E10]. This efficiency is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA ratio of 7.65x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 13.12x, suggesting the market has yet to fully price in the company's superior capital productivity [E11]. Market sentiment is beginning to shift, as evidenced by positive institutional money flow [E44] and a technical profile where the stock trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E34, E35], a high debtor period of 174 days [E61], and a recent decrease in promoter holding [E41, E62]. Despite these headwinds, the recent quarterly operating margin expansion of 5 percentage points [E31] confirms that the business is successfully capturing higher profitability, validating the potential for a sustained re-rating.

Arihant Capital Markets faces a significant valuation disconnect, as the current market price of ₹89.6 sits far above the DCF-derived intrinsic value of ₹49 per share, implying a margin of safety of -84.4% [E45, E46]. This premium is difficult to justify given that the company’s profit growth has stagnated, with a 5-year compounded profit growth of -2% and a 3-year growth of only 3% [E19, E20]. Furthermore, the company is struggling with capital efficiency, evidenced by a negative cash conversion of -3.94x and a substantial negative operating cash flow of Rs -122 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. The business also carries high operational risk, highlighted by high debtors of 174 days and a declining promoter stake, which has fallen by 3.96% over the last three years [E61, E62]. While the stock trades at a P/E of 19.84x, which exceeds the sector benchmark of 18.72x, the underlying ROE has deteriorated to 8% [E6, E29, E68]. Conceded: the company has shown strong recent sales and profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E17, E21, E66], and institutional money flow remains positive [E44].

The bear’s reliance on a DCF-derived intrinsic value of ₹49 [E45] ignores the company’s superior operational efficiency, as Arihant Capital delivers an ROA of 4.21% and an ROCE of 12.03%, both significantly outperforming sector benchmarks of 1.94% and 5.66% respectively [E8, E10]. While the bear highlights stagnant long-term profit growth, it overlooks the most recent evidence showing a 22% surge in trailing twelve-month sales and an 11% increase in profit growth [E17, E21], alongside a 62% year-over-year net profit jump [E66]. Conceded: the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -122 Cr in March 2026 [E35] and high debtors of 174 days [E61]. However, the bear’s focus on these figures ignores the positive institutional money flow [E44] and the fact that the stock is currently in a technical uptrend, trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. Furthermore, the company’s valuation is supported by an EV/EBITDA of 7.65x, which is substantially more attractive than the sector benchmark of 13.12x [E11]. Conceded: promoter holding has decreased by 3.96% over the last three years [E62]. Despite this, the company’s recent quarterly operating margin has expanded by 5 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], signaling a robust turnaround that stale sentiment fails to capture [E71].

Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales growth of 22% and a recent quarterly net profit jump [E17, E66]. However, the bull's dismissal of the DCF intrinsic value of ₹49 ignores the severe fundamental disconnect where today's price of ₹89.6 leaves an alarming margin of safety of -84.4% [E2, E45, E46]. Furthermore, while the bull points to outperforming ROCE and EV/EBITDA multiples, it glosses over the catastrophic cash destruction evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -122 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -3.94x in March 2026 [E35, E34]. Conceded: the stock trades above its moving averages [E50]. Yet this technical momentum directly contradicts the underlying multi-year stagnation featuring a 5-year compounded profit growth of -2% and a trailing ROE that has slumped to just 8% [E19, E29]. Finally, the bull's defense of management commitment fails to address the persistent insider distribution, evidenced by promoters actively reducing their stake by nearly 4% over the last three years [E62].
